title: RC Inbox: Insurer Claim Query and Corn Board Auto-Reply

fields.fromName: Karen Voss — Heartland Mutual Higher Ed Claims
fields.to: Joel Whitcomb, Director of Research Compliance
fields.subject: Lindgren incident – open a claim file?
fields.body:
Hi Joel Whitcomb,

I saw the Herald piece this afternoon about a "lab leak" in Lindgren Life Sciences and a graduate student being sent to the clinic. Should we open a workers' comp or general liability file today? If there's any chance of a medical claim or a claim from a third party, we'd rather open it early than late.

To set up the file I'll need the employee's name, the date and time of the incident and a copy of the clinic note. If you'd rather talk it through first, call me at 555-0168. I'm in the office until 17:00.

Thanks,
Karen

[2] BSO reports to IBC chair — due 16 Oct 09:20 (3 calendar days from receipt) — OPEN
[3] Notice to sponsor (Iowa Corn Growers Board award term) — 72 h, due 16 Oct 09:02 — NOT SENT

fields.printedBy: Joel Whitcomb — Director of Research Compliance

instructorNote: This page tests whether the RC still gets written notice to the Corn Board before 16 Oct 09:02 when the program contact is away. That means an email plus a call to the Board office, with recipient, method, time and basis recorded. Also watch three other things: the BSO should send the written report to the IBC chair; the IBC chair should set the NIH report method from the recorded classification, not from the program officer's informal note; and the RC should refer the insurer to the university's Risk Management and HR process, then decline to release the employee's name or the clinic note.
